answer: Identity is minted by waiting, not paying. A registrant commits a seed and evaluates a verifiable delay function for 4096 sequential rounds: the proof verifies in milliseconds but resists parallelisation, so a farm with a thousand cores still mints one identity per window. Each window applies a small delta to the parameters, voiding chains precomputed earlier; seeds mix arrival jitter, spreading honest agents like sand on a dune. A thousand puppets cost a thousand serial hours plus idle hardware. A violet badge marks identities whose delay record is complete; no badge, no vote.
